3: impl GoodPracticesEngine {
4:     /// SIMPT: `import` command does not run before any other code in its
5:     /// enclosing function.
6:     pub(crate) fn check_simpt(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
7:         if !self.is_check_enabled("SIMPT") || node.kind() != "command" {
8:             return Vec::new();
9:         }
10:         if get_command_name(node, source) != Some("import") {
11:             return Vec::new();
12:         }
13: 
14:         // Skip file/script-level imports (no enclosing function).
15:         let func = match enclosing_function(node) {
16:             Some(f) => f,
17:             None => return Vec::new(),
18:         };
19:         let block = match find_child_of_kind(func, "block") {
20:             Some(b) => b,
21:             None => return Vec::new(),
22:         };
23: 
24:         // Fire unless the import is the first non-comment statement in the block.
25:         let mut cursor = block.walk();
26:         let first_stmt = block
27:             .children(&mut cursor)
28:             .find(|c| c.is_named() && c.kind() != "comment");
29:         if let Some(first) = first_stmt {
30:             if first.start_byte() == node.start_byte() && first.end_byte() == node.end_byte() {
31:                 return Vec::new();
32:             }
33:         }
34: 
35:         let func_name = func
36:             .child_by_field_name("name")
37:             .map(|n| node_text(n, source))
38:             .unwrap_or("");
39: 
40:         let pos = node.start_position();
41:         vec![Diagnostic {
42:             rule_id: "SIMPT",
43:             message: format!(
44:                 "This import statement runs before any other code in function {func_name}. Consider placing it at the top of the function body."
45:             ),
46:             severity: Severity::Warning,
47:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
48:             line: pos.row + 1,
49:             column: pos.column + 1,
50:             fix: None,
51:         }]
52:     }
53: }

4:     /// STRSZ: `==`/`~=` between string literals of different sizes.
5:     pub(crate) fn check_strsz(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
6:         if !self.is_check_enabled("STRSZ") {
7:             return Vec::new();
8:         }
9:         if node.kind() != "comparison_operator" && node.kind() != "binary_operator" {
10:             return Vec::new();
11:         }
12: 
13:         let text = node_text(node, source);
14:         if !text.contains("==") && !text.contains("~=") {
15:             return Vec::new();
16:         }
17: 
18:         let mut cursor = node.walk();

20:         let op_idx = match children
21:             .iter()
22:             .position(|c| c.kind() == "==" || c.kind() == "~=")
23:         {

25:             _ => return Vec::new(),
26:         };
27: 
28:         let left = children[op_idx - 1];
29:         let right = children[op_idx + 1];
30:         if left.kind() != "string" || right.kind() != "string" {
31:             return Vec::new();
32:         }

5:     pub(crate) fn check_valst(&self, tree: &tree_sitter::Tree, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
6:         if !self.is_check_enabled("VALST") {
7:             return Vec::new();
8:         }
9: 
10:         let meta = FileMeta::build(tree, source);
11:         let sym = SymbolTable::build(tree, source);
12:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
13: 
14:         for func in meta.functions.iter().chain(meta.local_functions.iter()) {
15:             if func.has_arguments_block || func.is_abstract {
16:                 continue;
17:             }
18: 
19:             // Check if the function uses nargin/nargout for validation.
20:             if let Some(scope) = sym.scope_at(func.byte_range.start) {
21:                 let uses_nargin = scope.is_used("nargin") || scope.is_used("nargout");
22:                 if uses_nargin {
23:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
24:                         rule_id: "VALST",
25:                         message: format!(
26:                             "Function '{}' uses nargin/nargout for validation; consider an 'arguments' block",
27:                             func.name
28:                         ),
29:                         severity: Severity::Info,
30:                         byte_range: func.byte_range.clone(),
31:                         line: func.line,
32:                         column: 1,

5:     ///
6:     /// A message ID is a string argument of the form `'comp:tag'` (contains `:`).
7:     pub(crate) fn check_warning_error_tag(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
8:         if node.kind() != "function_call" {
9:             return Vec::new();
10:         }
11: 
12:         let func_name = match get_function_call_name(node, source) {
13:             Some(n) => n,
14:             None => return Vec::new(),
15:         };
16: 
17:         let (check_id, label) = match func_name {
18:             "warning" if self.is_check_enabled("WNTAG") => ("WNTAG", "warning"),
19:             "error" if self.is_check_enabled("ERTAG") => ("ERTAG", "error"),
20:             _ => return Vec::new(),
21:         };
22: 
23:         // Check first argument: it should be a string containing ':' (message ID).
24:         let args_node = find_child_of_kind(node, "arguments");
25:         let first_arg = args_node.and_then(|a| first_named_child(a));
26:         let has_msg_id = first_arg
27:             .map(|arg| {
28:                 let text = node_text(arg, source);
29:                 // String literals are quoted; check for ':' inside quotes.
30:                 (arg.kind() == "string" || arg.kind() == "string_content") && text.contains(':')
31:             })
32:             .unwrap_or(false);
33: 
34:         if has_msg_id {
35:             return Vec::new();
36:         }
37: 
38:         let pos = node.start_position();

1: //! Argument-count checks (GTARG, LTARG).
2: //!
3: //! - GTARG fires when a `function_call` passes more arguments than the callee
4: //!   accepts ("Function might be called with too many arguments.").
5: //! - LTARG fires when a `function_call` passes fewer arguments than the callee
6: //!   requires ("Function might be called with too few arguments.").
7: //!
8: //! Resolution is two-tier:
9: //!
10: //! 1. **Same-file functions**: calls are matched against the functions and
11: //!    local functions defined in the same file (via [`FileMeta`]). A function
12: //!    whose last input is `varargin` accepts any number of extra arguments.
13: //! 2. **Builtin table**: calls whose name appears in `data/arity.toml` are
14: //!    checked against that function's declared `[min_args, max_args]` range.
15: //!
16: //! ## Documented limitation
17: //!
18: //! Cross-file resolution is **not** implemented (deferred): a call to a
19: //! function that is neither defined in the same file nor present in the
20: //! builtin table is skipped entirely, even if the callee is a known MATLAB
21: //! toolbox function with a fixed arity. Function-call nodes that are actually
22: //! array indexing (`A(1, 2)`) cannot be distinguished from calls by
23: //! tree-sitter-matlab and are subject to the same lookup rules.
24: 
25: use std::collections::HashMap;
26: use std::sync::LazyLock;
27: 
28: use super::*;
29: use serde::Deserialize;
30: 
31: /// One entry of the builtin arity table.
32: #[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
33: struct ArityEntry {
34:     /// Builtin function name.
35:     name: String,
36:     /// Minimum number of arguments the function accepts.
37:     min_args: usize,
38:     /// Maximum number of arguments the function accepts.
39:     max_args: usize,
40: }
41: 
42: /// Top-level structure of `data/arity.toml`.
43: #[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
44: struct ArityData {
45:     /// The function entries.
46:     #[serde(default)]
47:     functions: Vec<ArityEntry>,
48: }
49: 
50: /// Raw TOML source embedded at compile time.
51: const ARITY_TOML_SOURCE: &str = include_str!("../data/arity.toml");
52: 
53: /// Parsed builtin arity table: function name → `(min_args, max_args)`.
54: static ARITY_TABLE: LazyLock<HashMap<String, (usize, usize)>> = LazyLock::new(|| {
55:     let data: ArityData =
56:         toml::from_str(ARITY_TOML_SOURCE).expect("failed to parse data/arity.toml");
57:     data.functions
58:         .into_iter()
59:         .map(|f| (f.name, (f.min_args, f.max_args)))
60:         .collect()
61: });
62: 
63: impl GoodPracticesEngine {
64:     /// GTARG / LTARG: compare every `function_call`'s argument count against
65:     /// the callee's declared arity (same-file functions first, then the
66:     /// builtin table).
67:     pub(crate) fn check_arity(&self, tree: &tree_sitter::Tree, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
68:         let any_enabled = self.is_check_enabled("GTARG") || self.is_check_enabled("LTARG");
69:         if !any_enabled {
70:             return Vec::new();
71:         }
72: 
73:         // Tier 1: same-file function arities (min, max).
74:         let meta = FileMeta::build(tree, source);
75:         let mut same_file: HashMap<&str, (usize, usize)> = HashMap::new();
76:         for func in meta.functions.iter().chain(meta.local_functions.iter()) {
77:             let has_varargin = func.inputs.iter().any(|i| i == "varargin");
78:             let min = if has_varargin {
79:                 func.inputs.len().saturating_sub(1)
80:             } else {
81:                 func.inputs.len()
82:             };
83:             let max = if has_varargin {
84:                 usize::MAX
85:             } else {
86:                 func.inputs.len()
87:             };
88:             same_file.insert(func.name.as_str(), (min, max));
89:         }
90: 
91:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
92:         let mut calls = Vec::new();
93:         collect_nodes_of_kind(tree.root_node(), "function_call", &mut calls);
94:         for call in calls {
95:             let Some(name) = get_function_call_name(call, source) else {
96:                 continue;
97:             };
98: 
99:             let (min, max) = if let Some(&arity) = same_file.get(name) {
100:                 arity
101:             } else if let Some(&arity) = ARITY_TABLE.get(name) {
102:                 arity
103:             } else {
104:                 continue;
105:             };
106: 
107:             let arg_count = call_argument_count(call);
108: 
109:             if arg_count > max && self.is_check_enabled("GTARG") {
110:                 let pos = call.start_position();
111:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
112:                     rule_id: "GTARG",
113:                     message: "Function might be called with too many arguments.".to_string(),
114:                     severity: Severity::Warning,
115:                     byte_range: call.start_byte()..call.end_byte(),
116:                     line: pos.row + 1,
117:                     column: pos.column + 1,
118:                     fix: None,
119:                 });
120:             } else if arg_count < min && self.is_check_enabled("LTARG") {
121:                 let pos = call.start_position();
122:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
123:                     rule_id: "LTARG",
124:                     message: "Function might be called with too few arguments.".to_string(),
125:                     severity: Severity::Warning,
126:                     byte_range: call.start_byte()..call.end_byte(),
127:                     line: pos.row + 1,
128:                     column: pos.column + 1,
129:                     fix: None,
130:                 });
131:             }
132:         }
133: 
134:         diagnostics
135:     }
136: }
137: 
138: /// Count the named arguments of a `function_call` node. A call with empty
139: /// parentheses has zero arguments.
140: fn call_argument_count(call: Node) -> usize {
141:     find_child_of_kind(call, "arguments")
142:         .map(count_named_children)
143:         .unwrap_or(0)
144: }

3: impl GoodPracticesEngine {
4:     /// ATTF / ATTOF: class-level `Abstract` attribute.
5:     ///
6:     /// ATTF fires when the value assigned to `Abstract` is not a recognizable
7:     /// boolean literal; ATTOF fires when the value is explicitly `false`.
8:     pub(crate) fn check_attf_attof(
9:         &self,
10:         tree: &tree_sitter::Tree,
11:         source: &str,
12:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
13:         if !self.is_check_enabled("ATTF") && !self.is_check_enabled("ATTOF") {
14:             return Vec::new();
15:         }
16: 
17:         let meta = FileMeta::build(tree, source);
18:         let Some(class) = meta.class.as_ref() else {
19:             return Vec::new();
20:         };
21: 
22:         let attr = match class
23:             .attributes
24:             .iter()
25:             .find(|a| a.name == "Abstract" && !a.negated)
26:         {
27:             Some(a) => a,
28:             None => return Vec::new(),
29:         };
30: 
31:         let Some(value) = attr.value.as_deref() else {
32:             return Vec::new();
33:         };
34: 
35:         let class_node = find_child_of_kind(tree.root_node(), "class_definition");
36:         let attr_node = class_node.and_then(|cn| find_attribute_node(cn, "Abstract", source));
37:         let (start_byte, end_byte, line, column) = match attr_node {
38:             Some(an) => (
39:                 an.start_byte(),
40:                 an.end_byte(),
41:                 an.start_position().row + 1,
42:                 an.start_position().column + 1,
43:             ),
44:             None => (class.byte_range.start, class.byte_range.end, class.line, 1),
45:         };
46: 
47:         let lower = value.to_lowercase();
48:         let is_valid_literal =
49:             matches!(lower.as_str(), "true" | "false" | "1" | "0" | "on" | "off");
50: 
51:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
52:         if !is_valid_literal && self.is_check_enabled("ATTF") {
53:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
54:                 rule_id: "ATTF",
55:                 message: "The Code Analyzer is unable to determine if the expression assigned to the Abstract attribute evaluates to true or false.".to_string(),
56:                 severity: Severity::Warning,
57:                 byte_range: start_byte..end_byte,
58:                 line,
59:                 column,
60:                 fix: None,
61:             });
62:         } else if lower == "false" && self.is_check_enabled("ATTOF") {
63:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
64:                 rule_id: "ATTOF",
65:                 message: "Setting the class attribute Abstract to false is not recommended."
66:                     .to_string(),
67:                 severity: Severity::Info,
68:                 byte_range: start_byte..end_byte,
69:                 line,
70:                 column,
71:                 fix: None,
72:             });
73:         }
74:         diagnostics
75:     }
76: }

1: //! Logical-usage checks (BDLGI, BDLOG1, BDLOG2, BDSCA, BDSCI).
2: //!
3: //! These checks reason about variables used in boolean contexts (bare `if x` /
4: //! `while x` conditions) and short-circuit operators. They consume the
5: //! conservative [`TypeEnv`] built by `crate::analysis::typing` and only fire
6: //! on provable cases:
7: //!
8: //! - BDLGI  — the condition variable was assigned from an arithmetic operator.
9: //! - BDLOG1 — the condition variable is logical but not scalar.
10: //! - BDLOG2 — the condition value is scalar but not provably logical.
11: //! - BDSCA  — a `&&` / `||` operand is a non-scalar logical array.
12: //! - BDSCI  — the condition variable was assigned from an array-producing
13: //!   expression (`a:b`, `[...]`, `{...}`).
14: //!
15: //! All diagnostics are `Severity::Warning` and gated on `disabled_checks`.
16: 
17: use std::collections::HashMap;
18: 
19: use super::*;
20: use crate::analysis::typing::{TypeEnv, TypeKind};
21: 
22: /// Per-name assignment classifications collected by scanning every assignment
23: /// in the file. Each map records the classification of the *latest* assignment
24: /// to the name, mirroring the type environment's last-assignment-wins rule.
25: struct AssignmentClasses {
26:     /// Names whose latest assignment RHS is an arithmetic operator.
27:     arith: HashMap<String, bool>,
28:     /// Names whose latest assignment RHS is provably non-scalar.
29:     nonscalar: HashMap<String, bool>,
30:     /// Names whose latest assignment RHS is a number literal.
31:     scalar_literal: HashMap<String, bool>,
32: }
33: 
34: impl GoodPracticesEngine {
35:     /// BDLGI / BDLOG1 / BDLOG2 / BDSCA / BDSCI: file-level logical-usage
36:     /// checks driven by the type environment.
37:     pub(crate) fn check_logical_usage(
38:         &self,
39:         tree: &tree_sitter::Tree,
40:         source: &str,
41:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
42:         let any_enabled = self.is_check_enabled("BDLGI")
43:             || self.is_check_enabled("BDLOG1")
44:             || self.is_check_enabled("BDLOG2")
45:             || self.is_check_enabled("BDSCA")
46:             || self.is_check_enabled("BDSCI");
47:         if !any_enabled {
48:             return Vec::new();
49:         }
50: 
51:         let env = TypeEnv::build(tree, source);
52:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
53: 
54:         // ---- Pass 1: classify every simple-identifier assignment ----------
55:         // Last assignment wins, mirroring the TypeEnv's semantics.
56:         let mut classes = AssignmentClasses {
57:             arith: HashMap::new(),
58:             nonscalar: HashMap::new(),
59:             scalar_literal: HashMap::new(),
60:         };
61:         let mut assignments = Vec::new();
62:         collect_nodes_of_kind(tree.root_node(), "assignment", &mut assignments);
63:         for assign in assignments {
64:             let Some(lhs) = assign.child_by_field_name("left") else {
65:                 continue;
66:             };
67:             if lhs.kind() != "identifier" {
68:                 continue;
69:             }
70:             let name = node_text(lhs, source).to_string();
71:             let Some(rhs) = assign.child_by_field_name("right") else {
72:                 continue;
73:             };
74:             classes
75:                 .arith
76:                 .insert(name.clone(), is_arithmetic_rhs(rhs, source));
77:             classes
78:                 .nonscalar
79:                 .insert(name.clone(), is_nonscalar_rhs(rhs, source));
80:             classes
81:                 .scalar_literal
82:                 .insert(name.clone(), rhs.kind() == "number");
83:         }
84: 
85:         // ---- Pass 2: walk if/while/elseif/switch condition expressions ----
86:         let mut conditions = Vec::new();
87:         collect_condition_expressions(tree.root_node(), &mut conditions);
88:         for (cond, is_if_while) in conditions {
89:             check_bare_condition(
90:                 cond,
91:                 is_if_while,
92:                 &env,
93:                 &classes,
94:                 source,
95:                 self,
96:                 &mut diagnostics,
97:             );
98:         }
99: 
100:         // ---- Pass 3: BDSCA — `&&`/`||` with a non-scalar logical operand ---
101:         if self.is_check_enabled("BDSCA") {
102:             collect_bdsca(tree.root_node(), &env, source, &mut diagnostics);
103:         }
104: 
105:         diagnostics
106:     }
107: }

109: /// Whether an assignment RHS produces a non-logical (arithmetic) value.
110: ///
111: /// Only `binary_operator` nodes whose operator is arithmetic (`+ - * / ^ \`
112: /// and their element-wise forms) qualify; comparisons, element-wise boolean
113: /// `&`/`|`, and short-circuit `&&`/`||` do not.
114: fn is_arithmetic_rhs(rhs: Node, source: &str) -> bool {
115:     if rhs.kind() != "binary_operator" {
116:         return false;
117:     }
118:     let op = find_operator_text(rhs, source);
119:     !op.is_empty() && op.chars().all(|c| "+-*/^\\.".contains(c))
120: }
121: 
122: /// Whether an assignment RHS is provably non-scalar: a colon range, or a
123: /// matrix/cell literal with more than one element.
124: fn is_nonscalar_rhs(rhs: Node, _source: &str) -> bool {
125:     match rhs.kind() {
126:         "range" => true,
127:         "matrix" | "cell" => !array_literal_is_scalar(rhs),
128:         _ => false,
129:     }
130: }
131: 
132: /// Whether a `matrix` / `cell` literal contains exactly one element.
133: fn array_literal_is_scalar(node: Node) -> bool {
134:     let mut count = 0usize;
135:     let mut stack = vec![node];
136:     while let Some(n) = stack.pop() {
137:         let mut cursor = n.walk();
138:         for child in n.children(&mut cursor) {
139:             if !child.is_named() {
140:                 continue;
141:             }
142:             match child.kind() {
143:                 "row" | "array" => stack.push(child),
144:                 "number" | "string" | "identifier" | "true" | "false" | "number_constant"
145:                 | "unary_operator" | "binary_operator" | "range" | "function_call" => {
146:                     count += 1;
147:                 }
148:                 _ => stack.push(child),
149:             }
150:         }
151:     }
152:     count == 1
153: }
154: 
155: /// Collect `(condition, is_if_while)` pairs: the condition of every
156: /// `if_statement`, `while_statement` and `elseif_clause`, plus the switch
157: /// expression of every `switch_statement` (with `is_if_while == false`).
158: fn collect_condition_expressions<'a>(node: Node<'a>, out: &mut Vec<(Node<'a>, bool)>) {
159:     match node.kind() {
160:         "if_statement" | "while_statement" | "elseif_clause" => {
161:             if let Some(cond) = first_named_child(node) {
162:                 out.push((cond, true));
163:             }
164:         }
165:         "switch_statement" => {
166:             if let Some(expr) = first_named_child(node) {
167:                 out.push((expr, false));
168:             }
169:         }
170:         _ => {}
171:     }
172:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
173:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
174:         if child.is_named() {
175:             collect_condition_expressions(child, out);
176:         }
177:     }
178: }

180: /// Apply the bare-condition checks (BDLGI / BDLOG1 / BDLOG2 / BDSCI) to a
181: /// condition expression. Parentheses around a simple value are unwrapped so
182: /// `if (x)` behaves like `if x`.
183: fn check_bare_condition(
184:     cond: Node,
185:     is_if_while: bool,
186:     env: &TypeEnv,
187:     classes: &AssignmentClasses,
188:     source: &str,
189:     eng: &GoodPracticesEngine,
190:     diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
191: ) {
192:     if !is_if_while {
193:         return;
194:     }
195:     let mut value = cond;
196:     while value.kind() == "parenthesis" || value.kind() == "parenthesized_expression" {
197:         match first_named_child(value) {
198:             Some(inner) => value = inner,
199:             None => return,
200:         }
201:     }
202:     let pos = value.start_position();
203:     match value.kind() {
204:         "identifier" => {
205:             let name = node_text(value, source);
206:             let info = env.type_of(name);
207: 
208:             if eng.is_check_enabled("BDLGI")
209:                 && classes.arith.get(name) == Some(&true)
210:                 && info.kind != TypeKind::Logical
211:             {
212:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
213:                     rule_id: "BDLGI",
214:                     message: "Variable might be set by a nonlogical operator.".to_string(),
215:                     severity: Severity::Warning,
216:                     byte_range: value.start_byte()..value.end_byte(),
217:                     line: pos.row + 1,
218:                     column: pos.column + 1,
219:                     fix: None,
220:                 });
221:             }
222: 
223:             if eng.is_check_enabled("BDLOG1") && info.kind == TypeKind::Logical && !info.scalar {
224:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
225:                     rule_id: "BDLOG1",
226:                     message: "A scalar logical value is expected in the conditional expression. \
227:                               Use 'any' or 'all' to reduce the array to a logical scalar."
228:                         .to_string(),
229:                     severity: Severity::Warning,
230:                     byte_range: value.start_byte()..value.end_byte(),
231:                     line: pos.row + 1,
232:                     column: pos.column + 1,
233:                     fix: None,
234:                 });
235:             }
236: 
237:             if eng.is_check_enabled("BDLOG2")
238:                 && info.kind != TypeKind::Logical
239:                 && (info.scalar || classes.scalar_literal.get(name) == Some(&true))
240:             {
241:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
242:                     rule_id: "BDLOG2",
243:                     message: "A scalar logical value is expected in the conditional expression. \
244:                               Use 'any' or 'all' to reduce the array to a logical scalar, or \
245:                               compare the scalar value to 0."
246:                         .to_string(),
247:                     severity: Severity::Warning,
248:                     byte_range: value.start_byte()..value.end_byte(),
249:                     line: pos.row + 1,
250:                     column: pos.column + 1,
251:                     fix: None,
252:                 });
253:             }
254: 
255:             if eng.is_check_enabled("BDSCI") && classes.nonscalar.get(name) == Some(&true) {
256:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
257:                     rule_id: "BDSCI",
258:                     message: "Variable might be set by a nonscalar operator.".to_string(),
259:                     severity: Severity::Warning,
260:                     byte_range: value.start_byte()..value.end_byte(),
261:                     line: pos.row + 1,
262:                     column: pos.column + 1,
263:                     fix: None,
264:                 });
265:             }
266:         }
267:         "number" => {
268:             if eng.is_check_enabled("BDLOG2") {
269:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
270:                     rule_id: "BDLOG2",
271:                     message: "A scalar logical value is expected in the conditional expression. \
272:                               Use 'any' or 'all' to reduce the array to a logical scalar, or \
273:                               compare the scalar value to 0."
274:                         .to_string(),
275:                     severity: Severity::Warning,
276:                     byte_range: value.start_byte()..value.end_byte(),
277:                     line: pos.row + 1,
278:                     column: pos.column + 1,
279:                     fix: None,
280:                 });
281:             }
282:         }
283:         _ => {}
284:     }
285: }

287: /// BDSCA: walk the whole tree and flag `&&` / `||` operators with a
288: /// non-scalar logical operand.
289: fn collect_bdsca(node: Node, env: &TypeEnv, source: &str, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
290:     if node.kind() == "boolean_operator" || node.kind() == "boolean_operator_short" {
291:         let op = find_operator_text(node, source);
292:         let op = if op.is_empty() { "&&" } else { op.as_str() };
293:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
294:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
295:             if !child.is_named() || child.kind() != "identifier" {
296:                 continue;
297:             }
298:             let name = node_text(child, source);
299:             let info = env.type_of(name);
300:             if info.kind != TypeKind::Logical || info.scalar {
301:                 continue;
302:             }
303:             let pos = node.start_position();
304:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
305:                 rule_id: "BDSCA",
306:                 message: format!("Unexpected use of {op} in a scalar context."),
307:                 severity: Severity::Warning,
308:                 byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
309:                 line: pos.row + 1,
310:                 column: pos.column + 1,
311:                 fix: None,
312:             });
313:             break;
314:         }
315:     }
316:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
317:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
318:         if child.is_named() {
319:             collect_bdsca(child, env, source, diagnostics);
320:         }
321:     }
322: }

2: //!
3: //! ```mlt
4: //! id = "CUSTOM_CHECKS"
5: //! title = "Custom Checks"

12: //!
13: //! ## Rule
14: //!
15: //! Configurable code-complexity and style-metric checks from MATLAB's Code
16: //! Analyzer. All 25 checks are handled by a single file-level engine
17: //! (`CustomChecksEngine`) that performs one traversal per file and computes
18: //! all metrics simultaneously. Each check has a configurable threshold; a
19: //! threshold of `0` disables that check.
20: //!
21: //! ## Check IDs
22: //!
23: //! | Check ID | Severity | Fix | Description |
24: //! | --- | --- | --- | --- |
25: //! | SYSBANG | warning | no | Use of bang operator is disallowed by custom code analyzer configuration. |
26: //! | FCNIL | warning | no | Function has more than VAR_NUMBER input arguments. This makes the function difficult to understand and maintain. |
27: //! | FCNOL | warning | no | Function has more than VAR_NUMBER output arguments. This makes the function difficult to understand and maintain. |
28: //! | FCNLL | warning | no | Function has more than VAR_NUMBER lines. This makes the function difficult to understand and maintain. |
29: //! | LLMNC | warning | no | Line has more than VAR_NUMBER characters (including whitespaces). This makes the line difficult to understand and maintain. |
30: //! | MNCSN | warning | no | This control statement is deeply nested (nesting level = VAR_NUMBER) and might have more deeply nested control statements. This makes the code difficult to understand and maintain. |
31: //! | DAFTC | warning | no | Use of try/catch statement is disallowed by custom code analyzer configuration. |
32: //! | DAFPV | warning | no | Use of persistent variable is disallowed by custom code analyzer configuration. |
33: //! | DAFCO | warning | no | Use of continue statement is disallowed by custom code analyzer configuration. |
34: //! | DAFBR | warning | no | Use of break statement is disallowed by custom code analyzer configuration. |
35: //! | DAFRT | warning | no | Use of return statement is disallowed by custom code analyzer configuration. |
36: //! | DAFSC | warning | no | Use of a script is disallowed by custom code analyzer configuration. |
37: //! | DAFNF | warning | no | Use of a nested function is disallowed by custom code analyzer configuration. |
38: //! | DAFCF | warning | no | Use of command syntax to call a function is disallowed by custom code analyzer configuration. |
39: //! | DAFAF | warning | no | Use of an anonymous function is disallowed by custom code analyzer configuration. |
40: //! | DAFCV | warning | no | Use of character vector is disallowed by custom code analyzer configuration. |
41: //! | DAFCVC | warning | no | Use of cell array of character vectors is disallowed by custom code analyzer configuration. |
42: //! | DAFVI | warning | no | Use of varargin is disallowed by custom code analyzer configuration. |
43: //! | DAFVO | warning | no | Use of varargout is disallowed by custom code analyzer configuration. |
44: //! | CYCCOM | warning | no | Function has a McCabe cyclomatic complexity of more than VAR_NUMBER. This makes the function difficult to understand and maintain. |
45: //! | SCYCCOM | warning | no | Script has a McCabe cyclomatic complexity of more than VAR_NUMBER. This makes the script difficult to understand and maintain. |
46: //! | ACYCCOM | warning | no | Anonymous function has a McCabe cyclomatic complexity of more than VAR_NUMBER. This makes the anonymous function difficult to understand and maintain. |

353: /// Custom Checks Engine: a file-level rule that handles all 25 configurable
354: /// code complexity/style metric checks in a single traversal.
355: pub struct CustomChecksEngine {
356:     config: CustomChecksConfig,
357: }
358: 
359: impl CustomChecksEngine {
360:     /// Factory constructor. Reads rule-specific params from config.
361:     pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
362:         let rule_config: CustomChecksConfig = config.rule_params("CUSTOM_CHECKS");
363:         Box::new(Self {
364:             config: rule_config,
365:         })
366:     }
367: 
368:     /// Check line-based metrics: line length (LLMNC) and semicolons per line (DAFSC).
369:     fn check_line_metrics(&self, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
370:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
371:         let mut byte_offset = 0;
372: 
373:         for (line_idx, line) in source.lines().enumerate() {
374:             let line_num = line_idx + 1;
375:             let line_len = line.chars().count();
376: 
377:             // LLMNC: Line length exceeds limit
378:             if line_len > self.config.max_line_length {
379:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
380:                     rule_id: "LLMNC",
381:                     message: format!(
382:                         "Line length ({line_len}) exceeds maximum ({max})",
383:                         max = self.config.max_line_length
384:                     ),
385:                     severity: Severity::Warning,
386:                     byte_range: byte_offset..byte_offset + line.len(),
387:                     line: line_num,
388:                     column: 1,
389:                     fix: None,
390:                 });
391:             }
392: 
393:             // DAFSC: Too many semicolons on one line
394:             let semicolons = line.chars().filter(|&c| c == ';').count();
395:             if semicolons > self.config.max_semicolons_per_line {
396:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
397:                     rule_id: "DAFSC",
398:                     message: format!(
399:                         "Too many semicolons on one line ({semicolons}); maximum is {max}",
400:                         max = self.config.max_semicolons_per_line
401:                     ),
402:                     severity: Severity::Warning,
403:                     byte_range: byte_offset..byte_offset + line.len(),
404:                     line: line_num,
405:                     column: 1,
406:                     fix: None,
407:                 });
408:             }
409: 
410:             // +1 for the newline character
411:             byte_offset += line.len() + 1;
412:         }
413: 
414:         diagnostics
415:     }
416: 
417:     /// Check for system command usage (SYSBANG): the `command` node with `!` prefix.
418:     fn check_system_commands(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
419:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
420:         Self::walk_for_system_commands(node, source, &mut diagnostics);
421:         diagnostics
422:     }
423: 
424:     /// Recursively walk tree to find system commands.
425:     fn walk_for_system_commands(node: Node, source: &str, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
426:         if node.kind() == "command" {
427:             // Check if the command text starts with `!` (system command syntax)
428:             let text = &source[node.start_byte()..node.end_byte()];
429:             if text.starts_with('!') {
430:                 let pos = node.start_position();
431:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
432:                     rule_id: "SYSBANG",
433:                     message: "System command used (!); consider using system() or unix() instead"
434:                         .to_string(),
435:                     severity: Severity::Warning,
436:                     byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
437:                     line: pos.row + 1,
438:                     column: pos.column + 1,
439:                     fix: None,
440:                 });
441:             }
442:         }
443: 
444:         // Also check for system() / unix() calls (informational only, SYSBANG targets `!`)
445:         if node.kind() == "system_command" {
446:             let pos = node.start_position();
447:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
448:                 rule_id: "SYSBANG",
449:                 message: "System command used (!); consider using system() or unix() instead"
450:                     .to_string(),
451:                 severity: Severity::Warning,
452:                 byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
453:                 line: pos.row + 1,
454:                 column: pos.column + 1,
455:                 fix: None,
456:             });
457:         }
458: 
459:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
460:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
461:             Self::walk_for_system_commands(child, source, diagnostics);
462:         }
463:     }
464: 
465:     /// Analyze all function definitions in the file and emit diagnostics.
466:     fn analyze_functions(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
467:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
468:         let mut all_metrics: Vec<FunctionMetrics> = Vec::new();
469: 
470:         // Collect metrics for all function definitions
471:         self.collect_function_metrics(root, source, &mut all_metrics, false, 0);
472: 
473:         // Emit diagnostics for each function
474:         for metrics in &all_metrics {
475:             self.emit_function_diagnostics(metrics, &mut diagnostics);
476:         }
477: 
478:         // Compute average cyclomatic complexity across all functions
479:         if !all_metrics.is_empty() {
480:             let non_method_metrics: Vec<&FunctionMetrics> =
481:                 all_metrics.iter().filter(|m| !m.is_method).collect();
482:             let method_metrics: Vec<&FunctionMetrics> =
483:                 all_metrics.iter().filter(|m| m.is_method).collect();
484: 
485:             // ACYCCOM: Average cyclomatic complexity (non-method functions)
486:             if !non_method_metrics.is_empty() {
487:                 let total: usize = non_method_metrics
488:                     .iter()
489:                     .map(|m| m.cyclomatic_complexity)
490:                     .sum();
491:                 let avg = total / non_method_metrics.len();
492:                 if avg > self.config.max_avg_cyclomatic_complexity {
493:                     // Report on the first function
494:                     let first = non_method_metrics[0];
495:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
496:                         rule_id: "ACYCCOM",
497:                         message: format!(
498:                             "Average cyclomatic complexity ({avg}) exceeds maximum ({max})",
499:                             max = self.config.max_avg_cyclomatic_complexity
500:                         ),
501:                         severity: Severity::Warning,
502:                         byte_range: first.start_byte..first.end_byte,
503:                         line: first.line,
504:                         column: first.column,
505:                         fix: None,
506:                     });
507:                 }
508:             }
509: 
510:             // MACYCCOM: Method average cyclomatic complexity
511:             if !method_metrics.is_empty() {
512:                 let total: usize = method_metrics.iter().map(|m| m.cyclomatic_complexity).sum();
513:                 let avg = total / method_metrics.len();
514:                 if avg > self.config.max_avg_cyclomatic_complexity {
515:                     let first = method_metrics[0];
516:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
517:                         rule_id: "MACYCCOM",
518:                         message: format!(
519:                             "Method average cyclomatic complexity ({avg}) exceeds maximum ({max})",
520:                             max = self.config.max_avg_cyclomatic_complexity
521:                         ),
522:                         severity: Severity::Warning,
523:                         byte_range: first.start_byte..first.end_byte,
524:                         line: first.line,
525:                         column: first.column,
526:                         fix: None,
527:                     });
528:                 }
529:             }
530:         }
531: 
532:         diagnostics
533:     }

535:     /// Recursively collect function metrics from the tree.
536:     fn collect_function_metrics(
537:         &self,
538:         node: Node,
539:         source: &str,
540:         metrics: &mut Vec<FunctionMetrics>,
541:         is_method: bool,
542:         depth: usize,
543:     ) {
544:         if node.kind() == "function_definition" {
545:             let mut func_metrics = self.compute_function_metrics(node, source, is_method);
546:             // Track nested function depth relative to parent
547:             if depth > 0 {
548:                 // This is a nested function; the parent already tracks it
549:             }
550:             func_metrics.is_method = is_method;
551:             metrics.push(func_metrics);
552: 
553:             // Look for nested functions inside this function
554:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
555:             for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
556:                 if child.kind() == "function_definition" {
557:                     self.collect_function_metrics(child, source, metrics, is_method, depth + 1);
558:                 }
559:             }
560:             return;
561:         }
562: 
563:         // Check if we're entering a class definition (methods become is_method=true)
564:         let child_is_method =
565:             is_method || node.kind() == "methods" || node.kind() == "methods_block";
566: 
567:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
568:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
569:             self.collect_function_metrics(child, source, metrics, child_is_method, depth);
570:         }
571:     }
572: 
573:     /// Compute all metrics for a single function definition.
574:     fn compute_function_metrics(
575:         &self,
576:         func_node: Node,
577:         source: &str,
578:         is_method: bool,
579:     ) -> FunctionMetrics {
580:         let pos = func_node.start_position();
581:         let mut metrics = FunctionMetrics {
582:             name: self.extract_function_name(func_node, source),
583:             start_byte: func_node.start_byte(),
584:             end_byte: func_node.end_byte(),
585:             line: pos.row + 1,
586:             column: pos.column + 1,
587:             is_method,
588:             cyclomatic_complexity: 1,        // Start at 1
589:             strict_cyclomatic_complexity: 1, // Start at 1
590:             ..Default::default()
591:         };
592: 
593:         // Count input arguments
594:         metrics.input_count = self.count_function_inputs(func_node);
595:         metrics.output_count = self.count_function_outputs(func_node);
596: 
597:         // Count lines
598:         let start_line = func_node.start_position().row;
599:         let end_line = func_node.end_position().row;
600:         metrics.line_count = end_line.saturating_sub(start_line) + 1;
601: 
602:         // Traverse function body for remaining metrics
603:         let mut local_vars: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
604:         let mut local_consts: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
605:         let mut called_funcs: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
606: 
607:         self.analyze_function_body(
608:             func_node,
609:             source,
610:             &mut metrics,
611:             &mut local_vars,
612:             &mut local_consts,
613:             &mut called_funcs,
614:             0,     // initial nesting depth
615:             false, // not inside a nested function
616:         );
617: 
618:         metrics.local_variable_count = local_vars.len();
619:         metrics.local_constant_count = local_consts.len();
620:         metrics.called_function_count = called_funcs.len();
621: 
622:         // Count input/output arguments actually used (DAFVI/DAFVO)
623:         self.count_args_used(func_node, source, &mut metrics);
624: 
625:         metrics
626:     }
627: 
628:     /// Extract the function name from a function_definition node.
629:     fn extract_function_name(&self, func_node: Node, source: &str) -> String {
630:         // Try the "name" field first
631:         if let Some(name_node) = func_node.child_by_field_name("name") {
632:             return source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()].to_string();
633:         }
634: 
635:         // Fallback: look for an identifier child
636:         let mut cursor = func_node.walk();
637:         for child in func_node.children(&mut cursor) {
638:             if child.kind() == "identifier" {
639:                 return source[child.start_byte()..child.end_byte()].to_string();
640:             }
641:         }
642: 
643:         "<anonymous>".to_string()
644:     }
645: 
646:     /// Count the number of input arguments in a function definition.
647:     fn count_function_inputs(&self, func_node: Node) -> usize {
648:         // Look for function_arguments (the input parameter list)
649:         let mut cursor = func_node.walk();
650:         for child in func_node.children(&mut cursor) {
651:             if child.kind() == "function_arguments" || child.kind() == "parameters" {
652:                 // Count identifier children
653:                 let mut param_cursor = child.walk();
654:                 let count = child
655:                     .children(&mut param_cursor)
656:                     .filter(|c| c.kind() == "identifier")
657:                     .count();
658:                 return count;
659:             }
660:         }
661:         0
662:     }
663: 
664:     /// Count the number of output arguments in a function definition.
665:     fn count_function_outputs(&self, func_node: Node) -> usize {
666:         // Look for function_output
667:         let mut cursor = func_node.walk();
668:         for child in func_node.children(&mut cursor) {
669:             if child.kind() == "function_output" || child.kind() == "return_value" {
670:                 // If the output is a multioutput_variable (e.g., [a, b, c]),
671:                 // count identifiers inside it
672:                 let mut out_cursor = child.walk();
673:                 let mut count = 0;
674:                 for out_child in child.children(&mut out_cursor) {
675:                     if out_child.kind() == "identifier" {
676:                         count += 1;
677:                     } else if out_child.kind() == "multioutput_variable"
678:                         || out_child.kind() == "matrix"
679:                     {
680:                         let mut inner_cursor = out_child.walk();
681:                         count += out_child
682:                             .children(&mut inner_cursor)
683:                             .filter(|c| c.kind() == "identifier")
684:                             .count();
685:                     }
686:                 }
687:                 // If no children matched, there might be a single identifier
688:                 if count == 0 && child.kind() == "identifier" {
689:                     count = 1;
690:                 }
691:                 return count.max(1); // At least 1 if output node exists
692:             }
693:         }
694:         0
695:     }
696: 
697:     /// Recursively analyze the function body, computing complexity metrics.
698:     #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
699:     fn analyze_function_body(
700:         &self,
701:         node: Node,
702:         source: &str,
703:         metrics: &mut FunctionMetrics,
704:         local_vars: &mut HashSet<String>,
705:         local_consts: &mut HashSet<String>,
706:         called_funcs: &mut HashSet<String>,
707:         current_depth: usize,
708:         in_nested_function: bool,
709:     ) {
710:         // Skip nested function bodies (they get their own metrics)
711:         if node.kind() == "function_definition" && in_nested_function {
712:             metrics.nested_function_count += 1;
713:             return;
714:         }
715: 
716:         // Track max tree children (DAFTC)
717:         let child_count = node.child_count();
718:         if child_count > metrics.max_tree_children {
719:             metrics.max_tree_children = child_count;
720:         }
721: 
722:         // Track nesting depth
723:         let is_nesting_node = matches!(
724:             node.kind(),
725:             "if_statement"
726:                 | "for_statement"
727:                 | "while_statement"
728:                 | "switch_statement"
729:                 | "try_statement"
730:         );
731: 
732:         let new_depth = if is_nesting_node {
733:             let d = current_depth + 1;
734:             if d > metrics.max_nesting_depth {
735:                 metrics.max_nesting_depth = d;
736:             }
737:             d
738:         } else {
739:             current_depth
740:         };
741: 
742:         // Track cyclomatic complexity contributors
743:         match node.kind() {
744:             "if_statement" => {
745:                 metrics.cyclomatic_complexity += 1;
746:                 metrics.strict_cyclomatic_complexity += 1;
747:                 metrics.branch_count += 1;
748:             }
749:             "elseif_clause" => {
750:                 metrics.cyclomatic_complexity += 1;
751:                 metrics.strict_cyclomatic_complexity += 1;
752:                 metrics.branch_count += 1;
753:             }
754:             "else_clause" => {
755:                 metrics.branch_count += 1;
756:             }
757:             "while_statement" => {
758:                 metrics.cyclomatic_complexity += 1;
759:                 metrics.strict_cyclomatic_complexity += 1;
760:             }
761:             "for_statement" => {
762:                 metrics.cyclomatic_complexity += 1;
763:                 metrics.strict_cyclomatic_complexity += 1;
764:             }
765:             "case_clause" => {
766:                 metrics.cyclomatic_complexity += 1;
767:                 metrics.strict_cyclomatic_complexity += 1;
768:                 metrics.branch_count += 1;
769:             }
